title: Claim Decomposition Map
summary: Break a broad answer into atomic factual, comparative, causal, predictive, and normative claims so each can receive the evidence and review it needs.
prerequisites: A draft answer, recommendation, or research question

sections.title: Separate claims before checking them
paragraphs: Split compound sentences until each row can be true or false on its own. Label observable facts, definitions, comparisons, causal explanations, forecasts, recommendations, and value judgments. A source that proves one row does not automatically prove the rows beside it.

Expose hidden qualifiers: who, what, when, where, version, population, baseline, and confidence. Mark calculations and inferences separately from quoted facts. If a conclusion depends on several premises, record the dependency so a failed premise invalidates the correct downstream claims.

sections.title: Worked case: a synthetic team pilot
paragraphs: Everything in this worked case is synthetic and is supplied only for practice. Training cohort T contains 40 analysts from one team. Independent comparison cohort V contains 40 different analysts from the same organization. Keeping the cohorts distinct resolves an apparent numerical conflict: 30 members of cohort T passed its post-test, while 16 plus 12, or 28, members of cohort V passed a separate comparison test. The records do not describe the same people or the same test administration.

Draft paragraph to audit: "During a two-week training pilot ending 2026-08-12, the same 40 analysts in cohort T took the same ten-item review test before and after training. Passes rose from 18 at baseline to 30 after training, so the pass rate rose from 45% to 75%, a 30 percentage-point increase and an approximately 66.7% relative increase. In a separate nonrandomized comparison cohort of 40 different analysts, 16 of 20 Tool A users passed and 12 of 20 Tool B users passed. Tool A is better and caused the pilot improvement. The team will reach a 90% pass rate next quarter, and leadership should mandate Tool A because productivity matters more than review time."

The paragraph mixes observations, calculations, an ambiguous general comparison, a causal explanation, a prediction, a recommendation, and a value judgment. Each must be tested separately. Even the two counts in one sentence must be separated because a changed source could contradict the baseline count while leaving the post-pilot count unchanged.
sections.callout: Do not add the cohort V passes to, or reconcile them arithmetically with, cohort T's post-test result. They are independent cohorts and test administrations.

sections.title: Supplied evidence excerpts and definitions
paragraphs: E-001, synthetic training-pilot record, dated 2026-08-12: "Population: cohort T, 40 analysts in one team. Design: the same analysts took the same ten-item review test immediately before and immediately after a two-week training pilot ending 2026-08-12. Baseline means the before-training administration. Baseline passes: 18 of 40. Post-pilot passes: 30 of 40. Tool use was not assigned or analyzed in this record."

E-002, synthetic tool-comparison record, dated 2026-08-12: "Population: independent comparison cohort V, 40 analysts who are not members of cohort T. Twenty used Tool A and twenty used Tool B for one administration of a parallel ten-item review test after standard orientation. Assignment was nonrandomized. Tool A passes: 16 of 20. Tool B passes: 12 of 20. No productivity, review-time, cost, safety, or accessibility measurements are recorded."

E-003, synthetic planning note, dated 2026-08-12: "The planning target is a 90% team pass rate next quarter. No next-quarter outcome has been observed. No validated forecast, forecasting model, or probability of reaching the target is supplied. The note does not rank productivity against review time and does not direct leadership to mandate either tool."

For this exercise, percentage-point change means subtracting one percentage from another. Relative percentage change means dividing the difference between the new and baseline percentages by the baseline percentage, then multiplying by 100. Baseline is the before-training administration identified in E-001.

DIRECT means the supplied excerpt or exact arithmetic states the scoped claim. INFERRED means the claim follows through an identified reasoning step but is not quoted directly. CONTRADICTED means the supplied evidence conflicts with the claim. UNKNOWN means the supplied material does not establish whether the claim is true or false. UNKNOWN is not the same as false.

A causal claim needs evidence capable of distinguishing the proposed cause from alternatives. The repeated test, time, other changes, and group selection are possible alternatives here. A recommendation proposes an action. A value judgment states or ranks what matters. The synthetic evidence IDs are local exercise sources and do not establish facts about any real organization.

sections.title: Build the map
paragraphs: Use safe identifiers for restricted evidence. Do not include private personal data, credentials, or confidential excerpts in a general-purpose research prompt.

Create one row for each independently falsifiable statement. A count and a percentage calculated from that count are separate rows. Two counts are separate rows. Percentage-point change and relative change are separate rows because either calculation can be wrong while the other is right.

Record the source that actually covers each row. A citation at the end of a paragraph cannot rescue distinct claims inside it. E-001 covers cohort T's design and counts, not cohort V's tool results. E-002 covers cohort V's observed counts, not a causal effect in cohort T. E-003 documents a target, not a forecast, mandate, or priority ranking.

code.label: Atomic claim map
code.code:
Claim ID: [C-001]
Atomic claim: [ONE CHECKABLE STATEMENT]
Type: [FACT | DEFINITION | COMPARISON | CAUSAL | PREDICTION | RECOMMENDATION | VALUE]
Scope: [WHO, WHAT, WHEN, WHERE, VERSION]
Materiality: [LOW | MEDIUM | HIGH]
Evidence needed: [OWNER DOC | DATA | EXPERIMENT | MULTIPLE SOURCES | EXPERT REVIEW]
Source or evidence ID: [URL OR SAFE ID]
Support: [DIRECT | INFERRED | CONTRADICTED | UNKNOWN]
Confidence and reason: [CALIBRATED STATEMENT]
Depends on: [OTHER CLAIM IDS]
Disposition: [KEEP | QUALIFY | REMOVE | ESCALATE]

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: The expected evidence is a complete map from each material statement to its source, inference, calculation, test, or unresolved status. Unsupported claims are removed, qualified, or escalated instead of being hidden behind one citation at paragraph end.

Read the draft sentence by sentence, confirm every checkable assertion has a row, open its evidence, recompute derived values, and trace dependencies. Ask a reviewer to find one unsupported qualifier, one source that only partially supports its claim, and one plausible contradiction.

Verification also requires scope fidelity. Cohort T and cohort V are different populations. A direct observation in cohort V cannot silently become an explanation of a change in cohort T. Dates, test administration, assignment method, denominator, baseline, and rounding all remain visible in the map.

sections.title: Exact calculations
paragraphs: CALC-001: 18 divided by 40 equals 0.45, or 45%. CALC-002: 30 divided by 40 equals 0.75, or 75%. CALC-003: 75% minus 45% equals 30 percentage points.
CALC-004: ((75 minus 45) divided by 45) multiplied by 100 equals 66.666...%. The rendered claim uses approximately 66.7% because it is rounded to one decimal place.
CALC-005: 16 divided by 20 equals 0.80, or 80%. CALC-006: 12 divided by 20 equals 0.60, or 60%. CALC-007: 80% minus 60% equals 20 percentage points.

code.label: Calculation records
code.code:
CALC-001: 18 / 40 = 0.45 = 45%; source E-001
CALC-002: 30 / 40 = 0.75 = 75%; source E-001
CALC-003: 75% - 45% = 30 percentage points; depends on CALC-001 and CALC-002
CALC-004: ((75 - 45) / 45) x 100 = 66.666...%, rounded to approximately 66.7%; depends on CALC-001 and CALC-002
CALC-005: 16 / 20 = 0.80 = 80%; source E-002
CALC-006: 12 / 20 = 0.60 = 60%; source E-002
CALC-007: 80% - 60% = 20 percentage points; depends on CALC-005 and CALC-006

sections.title: Completed atomic map for the worked case
paragraphs: C-001 through C-012 preserve the scoped observations and arithmetic. C-013 removes the unsupported general claim that Tool A is better. C-014 rejects the causal shortcut. C-015 through C-017 expose the unsupported forecast, recommendation, and value judgment. C-018 retains the narrower inference that the cohort T result is compatible with training helping but does not identify a causal effect.

C-002 is only the baseline count. C-003 is only the post-pilot count. C-006 is only the percentage-point change. C-007 is only the relative change. This atomic form allows a later contradiction to affect the exact premises and descendants that rely on it.

sections.title: Why the causal shortcut is rejected
paragraphs: C-014 links Tool A in cohort V to an increase measured in cohort T. The populations and test administrations are different, and E-001 does not identify tool use. That cross-cohort jump is unsupported even before considering nonrandom assignment.

Within cohort T, the before-and-after observation establishes temporal order and an observed difference, but not the counterfactual result that would have occurred without training. Repeating the same test, unrelated changes over the two weeks, measurement effects, and other explanations remain possible. The correct disposition is to remove the claim that Tool A caused the improvement and retain the qualified C-018 inference.

sections.title: Correct the paragraph without overclaiming
paragraphs: Supported revision: "In the synthetic training pilot ending 2026-08-12, the same 40 analysts in cohort T took the same ten-item review test before and after two weeks of training. Eighteen of 40 passed at baseline, a 45% pass rate. Thirty of 40 passed after the pilot, a 75% pass rate. The observed increase was 30 percentage points, or approximately 66.7% relative to baseline. This result is compatible with training helping, but the pre/post design does not establish that training caused the increase. In independent cohort V, which contained 40 different analysts, 16 of 20 Tool A users passed, or 80%, and 12 of 20 Tool B users passed, or 60%, in a nonrandomized comparison. Tool A's observed pass rate was 20 percentage points higher in those groups, but the evidence does not establish general superiority or causation. A 90% next-quarter pass rate is a target, not a supported forecast. A tool mandate requires additional evidence about productivity, review time, cost, safety, accessibility, group comparability, and stakeholder priorities."

The correction preserves direct observations, exact denominators, cohort boundaries, calculations, and a labeled inference. It removes the unsupported causal conclusion and general superiority claim. It also distinguishes a target from a prediction and a measured outcome from a normative decision.

sections.title: Independent changed-input task
paragraphs: Complete this task before reading the hints or answer key. Replace only E-001 with E-001B. E-001B, synthetic training-pilot record, dated 2026-08-12: "Population: cohort T, 40 analysts in one team. Design: the same analysts took the same ten-item review test immediately before and immediately after a two-week training pilot ending 2026-08-12. Baseline means the before-training administration. Baseline passes: 30 of 40. Post-pilot passes: 30 of 40. Tool use was not assigned or analyzed in this record."

E-002 and E-003 remain unchanged. Cohort V is still independent of cohort T. Identify the one original observational premise directly contradicted by E-001B, recompute all affected values, and trace the consequences through dependencies. Preserve unrelated supported claims.

Learner deliverables: an atomic claim list; calculation records; a complete dependency-aware map using every template field; the support and disposition for each changed or preserved claim; a corrected paragraph; and two sentences explaining why E-002 cannot repair a contradicted premise about cohort T.

Do not solve the task by deleting the whole map. The changed baseline can invalidate some descendants while leaving the post-pilot count, study design, independent tool counts, and scoped tool comparison supported.

sections.title: Hints for the changed-input task
paragraphs: Hint 1: C-001 and C-003 remain directly supported. The directly contradicted original premise is C-002, which said that 18 analysts passed at baseline.
Hint 2: Create C-002B for the changed baseline count, C-004B for its percentage, C-006B for the percentage-point change, and C-007B for the relative change.

Hint 3: 30 divided by 40 is 75% at both time points. The percentage-point change is 75% minus 75%, or 0 percentage points. The relative change is ((75 minus 75) divided by 75) multiplied by 100, or 0%.

Hint 4: Claims C-008 through C-012 concern independent cohort V and remain supported. C-014 remains unsupported, but its reason becomes even clearer because cohort T has no observed increase under E-001B.

sections.title: Answer map and feedback for the changed-input task
paragraphs: The old C-002 is CONTRADICTED and REMOVE because E-001B states 30 baseline passes, not 18. C-002B is DIRECT and KEEP. The old baseline-rate C-004, increase C-006, relative-change C-007, and qualified increase claim C-018 must be replaced because they depend on the contradicted premise.

C-001, C-003, and C-005 remain directly supported. C-008 through C-012 remain supported by E-002 because they concern independent cohort V. C-013 remains UNKNOWN and REMOVE. C-014 remains UNKNOWN and REMOVE. C-015 remains UNKNOWN and ESCALATE. C-016 remains UNKNOWN and QUALIFY. C-017 remains UNKNOWN and ESCALATE.

Two-sentence explanation: E-002 cannot repair C-002 because E-002 describes different analysts in independent cohort V and does not state cohort T's baseline count. Its nonrandomized tool comparison also cannot create a pre/post increase or causal result in cohort T.

Corrected changed-input paragraph: "In the changed synthetic record, the same 40 analysts in cohort T took the same ten-item review test before and after the two-week pilot. Thirty of 40 passed at baseline, or 75%, and 30 of 40 passed after the pilot, also 75%. The observed change was 0 percentage points and 0% relative to baseline. These data show no observed pass-rate change and do not establish that training caused an increase. Separately, in independent cohort V, 16 of 20 Tool A users passed, or 80%, and 12 of 20 Tool B users passed, or 60%, in a nonrandomized comparison. Tool A had the higher observed pass rate in those groups, but this does not establish general superiority, causation, or a 90% next-quarter outcome. A mandate still requires additional decision evidence and explicit stakeholder priorities."

sections.title: Save-as file: claim_maps.json
paragraphs: Save the code block exactly as claim_maps.json in a local working directory. It is a learner-visible fixture containing the complete worked and changed maps. The changed map deliberately retains old C-002 as a contradicted row so the premise contradiction is traceable.

The expectedIds lists define complete claim coverage for this exercise. Missing and extra claim IDs are structural failures. The checker does not decide whether the prose semantically follows from the evidence.

sections.title: Save-as file: checker.py
paragraphs: Save the code block as checker.py beside claim_maps.json. It uses only the Python standard library. It validates top-level and nested shapes, required and extra fields, allowed enum values, nonempty and duplicate IDs, exact expected claim coverage, dependency references, and dependency cycles. It also requires a nonempty evidence identifier for every MEDIUM or HIGH material claim.

Enum validation first checks that a value is a string and then checks set membership. This keeps malformed list, dictionary, and null values inside the controlled validation path instead of allowing a TypeError from an unhashable set-membership operand. The materiality evidence gate applies the same string guard.

The checker does not verify semantic entailment, arithmetic, source authenticity, URL resolution, live evidence, causal validity, or whether a recommendation is wise. No actual execution is claimed in this resource.

The implementation uses json.load and JSONDecodeError handling from the Python standard library documentation at https://docs.python.org/3/library/json.html, deepcopy for isolated self-test mutations at https://docs.python.org/3/library/copy.html#copy.deepcopy, isinstance type checks at https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#isinstance, and open, sys.argv, and sys.exit as documented at https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#open and https://docs.python.org/3/library/sys.html.

Run the fixture check with: python3 checker.py claim_maps.json. Run the fixture check plus meaningful negative cases with: python3 checker.py claim_maps.json --self-test. On systems where the Python 3 command is python, substitute python for python3.

code.label: checker.py

sections.title: Expected checker output
paragraphs: For python3 checker.py claim_maps.json, the expected standard output is the single PASS line shown below. This is an expected result, not a claim that the command was actually executed while preparing this resource.

For python3 checker.py claim_maps.json --self-test, the expected standard output is the PASS line followed by the SELF-TEST PASS line. The self-test contains the original 10 negative cases plus 12 additional assertions: list, dictionary, and null values for each of Type, Materiality, Support, and Disposition. These malformed values must produce validation diagnostics rather than a TypeError.

sections.title: Common errors and feedback
paragraphs: Error: treating the cohort T post-test count of 30 and cohort V's combined 28 passes as conflicting measurements. Feedback: the evidence explicitly identifies different cohorts and test administrations. Preserve that scope in every row.

Error: writing one claim that combines baseline and post-pilot counts. Feedback: use C-002 and C-003 separately. E-001B demonstrates why, because it changes the baseline while preserving the post-pilot count.

Error: combining percentage-point and relative changes. Feedback: C-006 and C-007 are separate. Thirty percentage points is an absolute difference between rates; approximately 66.7% is a change relative to the 45% baseline.
Error: citing E-001 for cohort V's tool comparison. Feedback: E-001 concerns cohort T. E-002 alone supplies the Tool A and Tool B observations.

Error: allowing the citation at the paragraph end to support every statement. Feedback: each factual count, calculation, causal explanation, forecast, recommendation, and value judgment has different evidence needs. Map each one explicitly.

Error: changing an observed association into causation. Feedback: cohort V assignment was nonrandomized, and cohort V is not cohort T. Neither record identifies Tool A as the cause of cohort T's change.
Error: treating the 90% target as a forecast. Feedback: E-003 explicitly supplies no validated forecast or probability.
Error: treating UNKNOWN as false. Feedback: UNKNOWN means the supplied evidence does not decide the claim. Remove, qualify, or escalate it according to materiality and use.
Error: deleting all claims after E-001 changes. Feedback: trace dependencies. The cohort V claims remain supported because E-002 did not change.

sections.title: Provider-neutral transfer
paragraphs: Apply the same process to reports, spreadsheets, dashboards, retrieval systems, classifiers, generative systems, search tools, policy memos, experiments, and human-authored recommendations. Separate observations from calculations, calculations from inferences, and inferences from decisions.

The method does not depend on a particular vendor, model, interface, or deployment. For any system, expose the population, version, date, task, baseline, comparison condition, outcome, and uncertainty. Then map each claim to the evidence that covers that exact scope.

Provider documentation can explain a product or evaluation method, but it does not automatically establish performance in a local deployment. Local outcome claims still require local evidence with traceable conditions and measurements.

sections.title: Source fidelity and limits
paragraphs: The three public links below are retained as first-party resources on AI risk management and evaluation practice. They do not prove any synthetic cohort count, arithmetic result, causal conclusion, forecast, recommendation, or value judgment in this exercise.

The NIST source is published by NIST. The evaluation guides are official documentation from OpenAI and Anthropic. Their listed verification dates are preserved from the supplied resource metadata. No new live-source verification is claimed here.

The offline checker is deliberately narrower than human review. Passing it establishes only conformance to its displayed structural rules. A reviewer must still inspect source meaning, arithmetic, scope, causal design, uncertainty, privacy, and decision tradeoffs.
